## Diverging Signals
- **VIX and VXN point in opposite directions, and the dates differ.** VIX is 29.96 (−16.52%, dated 2026-11-23) while VXN is 45.25 (+24.04%, dated 2026-11-20). VXN is the Nasdaq-100 version of VIX. The term-ratio table puts VIX at 38.48 on the Friday close. So VIX likely fell from about 38.5 to 30.0 between the Friday close and today's read. That means fear in the broad market eased while the Nasdaq-100 has not been repriced. I cannot say whether this is a real calming or a data-timing gap. Treat it as unresolved.
- **Yields are falling while stocks crash.** The 10Y fell 2.77% to 4.912%. In a rate-fear sell-off, yields rise. A fall means money is moving to bonds, which fits a growth scare more than an inflation scare. The Bloomberg headline about the Fed-hike trade being "roiled" fits this.
- **Gold rose 3.02% and Brent fell 4.59%.** Haven demand is back, and oil is easing. This partly contradicts the Iran-war headline pressure.
- **Options traders are not panicking.** Put/call is 0.55. After a 15.94% one-day fall, calls still outnumber puts. That is dip-buying behaviour (or call-heavy positioning from before the fall), not capitulation. It is at odds with VXN at 45.25 and VVIX at 138.03.
- **RSI 30.6 sits right at oversold, but that lags a one-day 16% fall.** It does not prove a low.
- What the tension implies: price and volatility say crisis, while put/call and the falling VIX say the crisis is not yet being priced everywhere. Both can be true for a day or two, but it is an unstable mix.

## TQQQ Read
- Momentum: **Neutral, at the oversold edge.** RSI is 30.6, just above 30, after a 15.94% one-day fall. The reading lags. For a put seller, oversold with a rising-volatility backdrop can mean rich premium, but this is not a stabilising low yet. Premium versus realized movement is roughly fair: IV/HV is 0.92 (HV20 114.7%).
- Market structure: **DOWNTURN.** Spot ($41.20) is 43.2% under the $72.53 4-week high ($41.20 / $72.53 = 0.568), past the 20% line. VXN is 45.25, past the 25 line. Both legs are met. Spot is 2.7% above the 4-week low ($41.20 / $40.12 = 1.027), far short of the 30% line for RALLY.
- Trend: below the 50DMA by 40.08% and below the 200DMA by 37.1%. Spot is 53.03% under the 52-week high and 10.9% above the 52-week low.
- Volatility & premium environment: VXN is 45.25 (+24.04%), 7.2% under its 52-week high of 48.74. Chain ATM IV is 1.05 (105%) and IV/HV is 0.92 (HV20 114.7%). IV/HV under 1 means options cost slightly less than the stock has been moving, so sellers get no extra cushion even at very high absolute levels. Chain IV of 105% is about 23% under the ~136% implied by the 3x-VXN rule of thumb (estimate only). VVIX at 138.03 says volatility itself is unstable. Premium is rich in dollars, but swing risk is extreme.
- Put-selling context: HOSTILE. The stage is 5, all seven lenses are bearish, spot sits 2.7% above its 4-week low and 10.9% above its 52-week low, and both credit lines are broken. The volatility curve is in deep backwardation (1.187) and VXN is near its 52-week high. A one-week expected move of about ±16% is very wide for a stock this close to a fresh low. A 15.94% one-day move shows the gap risk is real and not hypothetical. Context only — no strikes, expiries or sizes.
